h1:
Lopburi 1-Day Itinerary
Monkeys, Royal Palace & Local Eats
intro: Lopburi really is a town you can see in a single day, because the main historic sites — Prang Sam Yot, King Narai's Palace, Vichayen House and Phra Kan Shrine — all sit within walking distance of each other in the old town. The streets around them are packed with long-running eateries too. Here's a plan that covers the ruins, the monkeys and the good food, all in one day.

blocks.html: The nice thing about Lopburi is that everything clusters near the train station. If you take the train from Bangkok (about two and a half hours), you can start sightseeing on foot the moment you step off — no need to rent a car. And if you drive yourself, you can just park around the old town and loop through it on foot. This plan is an easy single day: start in the morning, wrap up by evening, with time to spare for photos and for stopping to eat along the way.

blocks.title: What to know about the monkeys first
blocks.html: The Lopburi monkeys are densest around Prang Sam Yot and Phra Kan Shrine. They're quick and love to grab things — take off your glasses, hold onto your hat, and keep plastic bags and water bottles tucked away. Don't carry food as you walk past, and don't make eye contact for too long. King Narai's Palace and Vichayen House, on the other hand, barely have any monkeys, so you can stroll there in peace.

items.activity: Start at Prang Khaek and the street art nearby
items.note: Prang Khaek is an old Khmer shrine right in the centre of town, and the area around it has colourful street-art murals for photos. The morning sun is still mild, so it's a comfortable walk.

A palace from the reign of King Narai the Great, blending Thai and Western architecture by French builders. The Somdet Phra Narai National Museum sits within the palace grounds — easily about an hour and a half of relaxed wandering.

The old European-style house of Constantine Phaulkon (Chao Phraya Wichayen). The ancient brick ruins and an old Christian church give it a different feel from the rest of town. Around 30–40 minutes to explore.

Long-established shops cluster near the train station and the municipal market. You can pick chicken rice, tom yum noodles, or duck rice (see our picks below). Some shops sell out before the afternoon, so if you want to be sure, get there before noon.

items.activity: Coffee and dessert to cool down
items.note: The Lopburi afternoon sun gets pretty hot. Stop at a café or one of the old-school fresh-milk shops in town and rest for an hour or so before the afternoon stretch.
A large central prang and the ruins of cloistered galleries, sitting right across from the train station. It's a lovely spot for ruin photos and far less crowded than Prang Sam Yot.

items.activity: Prang Sam Yot and Phra Kan Shrine
items.note: The highlight of monkey town: three Khmer Bayon-style prangs in a row, with loads of monkeys around. Across the way is Phra Kan Shrine, where people come to make merit and wishes. Watch your valuables carefully here.

items.activity: Walk the market and grab souvenirs before heading back
items.note: Lopburi is known for firm, meaty custard apples, dried chalk (din so phong), crispy mee krob and old-style khanom buang. Pick up a few before catching the train or driving home.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Lopburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

blocks.text: Old-town eateries that locals actually go to

blocks.html: Part of Lopburi's charm is the decades-old shops, most of them in the old-town area near the train station — close enough to walk or take a short ride between them. We've picked places that get steady reviews and are still open, sorted to match the timing of the plan.

items.name: Tan Roast Duck Rice
items.blurb: A long-running roast-duck shop behind the district office. The duck is tender and the gravy is fragrant and well-balanced. Open mornings until noon only, so it's a great late breakfast before tackling the ruins.

items.name: Dome Chicken Rice
items.blurb: A famous chicken-rice shop across from Lotus's on Phahonyothin Road. Tender chicken, fragrant rice, a punchy dipping sauce — an easy, filling lunch. Open late into the evening, closed Mondays.
items.meta: Phahonyothin Rd, across from Lotus's · Tue–Sun 10:00–20:00

items.name: Chaloem Thai Tom Yum Noodles
items.blurb: A small shop near Wat Phrommat serving bold tom yum noodles, with a sour-spicy broth that Lopburi locals are hooked on. Open morning to afternoon, closed Fridays.

items.name: 12-Baht Boat Noodles
items.blurb: Small-bowl boat noodles at a friendly price, on the lane toward Wat Khok Muang. The queue gets fairly long in the late morning, and you can order several bowls since the small portions go down easy.

items.name: Chatnara
items.blurb: A Thai restaurant on Phraya Kamjat Road with a varied menu — squid stir-fried with salted egg, plus local-style curries. A good spot for dinner when you want to order several dishes to share.

items.name: Lopburi Old-Style Khanom Buang (Sala Chaloem Thai, est. 1954)
items.blurb: Old-style khanom buang with a thin, crisp shell, in both sweet and savoury fillings — a recipe dating back to 1954. Grab some to snack on while you wander, or to take home as a gift.

blocks.title: Timing tip
blocks.html: Several of Lopburi's famous shops are morning-to-afternoon places — duck rice and boat noodles often sell out before the afternoon. If you have your eye on a particular spot, slotting it into the midday part of the plan is the safer bet. Save the dinner meal for places that stay open late.

items.name: Lopburi custard apples
items.blurb: Lopburi is a growing region for firm, meaty, sweetly fragrant custard apples. They're easy to find at markets and fruit shops in town, and they're fresh and cheap in season.

items.name: Din so phong (chalk powder)
items.blurb: A traditional Lopburi product made from good-quality marl clay — a souvenir you can really only find in this town.

items.name: Mee krob & old-style khanom buang
items.blurb: Snacks that keep well, so they travel home easily on the train. Look for them at souvenir shops in the old-town area.

items: Train from Bangkok — leaving from Hua Lamphong/Bang Sue, it's about two and a half hours to Lopburi. Step off the train and you can start exploring the old town right away — ideal for a no-car day trip.
Driving yourself — about 150 km from Bangkok, around two hours. Park near the old town and loop through on foot — it's easier than driving in and out of several spots.

What to wear — some historic sites call for modest dress. Wear comfortable walking shoes since there's a lot of walking, and bring a hat and water because the midday-to-afternoon sun is fairly strong.
Entry fees — the main historic sites charge a small fee of a few tens of THB each; some have a combined ticket. Keep small cash on hand for convenience.

faq.q: What can you do in Lopburi in one day?
faq.a: You can see it all in a single day because the main historic sites are close together. Start at Prang Khaek and the street art, then King Narai's Palace and Vichayen House. In the afternoon, head to Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, Prang Sam Yot and Phra Kan Shrine, and finish with some souvenir shopping.

faq.q: Do you need to watch out for monkeys in Lopburi?
faq.a: Be careful around Prang Sam Yot and Phra Kan Shrine, where the monkeys are densest. They like to grab things, so keep your glasses, hat, water bottle and plastic bags tucked away, and don't walk past carrying food. King Narai's Palace and Vichayen House barely have any monkeys.

faq.q: Is taking the train to Lopburi a good idea?
faq.a: It's great for a day trip. The train from Bangkok takes about two and a half hours, and the station sits right by the old town. Step off and you can explore the ruins and eat well without renting a car.

faq.q: What Lopburi food should you try?
faq.a: Duck rice at Tan, chicken rice at Dome, tom yum noodles at Chaloem Thai, and small-bowl boat noodles. For souvenirs, go for Lopburi custard apples, old-style khanom buang and din so phong (chalk powder).

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Lopburi?
faq.a: You can tour the old town year-round, but if you want to catch the sunflower fields in bloom, go from late in the year to early the next (roughly November–January). For walking around town, start early to avoid the midday-to-afternoon heat.
